messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High-rate anomaly detected on embeddings proxy cluster (embed-proxy-*). Traffic 6.2x baseline, many short-lived tokens and identical UA. Incident INC-2026-042 created.
maria: seeing huge 429s coming from embed-proxy-02 in eu-west-1, KV cache thrash + prefix cold misses.
kevin: traffic fingerprint: user-agent "embed-fetcher/1.2" + missing referer; bursts from ~1200 distinct /16s. Looks botlike, likely scrape farm.
oncall-ryan: I'm oncall, jumping in. Can someone paste top IPs + sample headers?
maria: top IPs (truncated):
```
198.51.100.23
203.0.113.45
198.51.100.56
45.168.12.101
```
kevin: confirmed repeated short-lived tokens, many requests with identical prompt shapes. Proposing immediate mitigations: 1) tighten per-IP and per-key QPS on embedding endpoints 2) apply WAF UA block for "embed-fetcher/1.2" 3) disable embeddings async batch endpoint for non-auth'd clients.
oncall-ryan: agree. I'll apply rate policy with a small blast radius then escalate if stable. Rolling to eu region first.
sre-lead: prefer canary: 25% of edge nodes in eu-west with hard limits (3 qps) and WAF rule. If stable for 10m, expand.
maria: canary applied to eu-west cluster (nodes 2-5) with policy tight-embeds (3 qps per API key, 5 req/s per IP).
kevin: pushed WAF rule wf-924 to block UA "embed-fetcher/1.2" and known malicious IPs (198.51.100.0/24).
eng-runtime: temporarily set embeddings-batch.max_batch_size=8 and disabled async_job_queue for anonymous keys. config snippet:
```json
{"embeddings_batch":{"max_batch_size":8,"async_jobs_enabled":false}}
```
cm-ops: noting downstream impact: some low-volume customers may see increased latencies and 429s. Which customers hit hardest?
support-jen: AcmeCorp and notifier-prod seeing spikes; raising priority-1 support tickets and sending initial customer notice. Draft note: "We're mitigating abnormal traffic which may cause rate-limited embeddings. We're prioritizing availability; temporary throttles may return 429s." :loudspeaker:
oncall-ryan: initial telemetry: error rate peaked at +18% 429s for embeddings, CPU on embed-proxy at 93% before canary. After canary, CPU down to 64% in canary nodes.
sre-lead: expand the policy to ap-south-1 at +20% traffic distribution. Keep eu-west at canary for another 8m.
kevin: also added short-term token blacklisting for obviously compromised tokens (token pattern match). Implemented TTL=5m.
eng-runtime: rolling rollback plan ready: command `redwood infra rollback-config embeddings-batch` if latencies spike >150ms P95.
cm-ops: do we want to disable bulk-embedding endpoint entirely? That'll impact partners. Maybe only for free-tier keys.
maria: yes, we disabled bulk endpoint for anonymous and free-tier keys in eu-west canary.
support-jen: customer update posted to status page: "Investigating abnormal embedding traffic; protective throttles in place. Some requests may return 429s. We'll update as we mitigate." Link -> https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042
incident-bot: UPDATE 6:13 UTC: canary nodes show 2.7x baseline (down from 6.2x), 429s persist at reduced rate, no increase in 5xx.
lee-sre: taking next handoff in 25m. please DM me a 1-2 line summary and the action list.
oncall-ryan: summary for handoff -> actions taken: canary eu-west, WAF rule wf-924, rate policy tight-embeds (3 qps/key, 5 req/s/IP), async batch disabled for anon/free, token blacklist TTL=5m. Telemetry: traffic reduced to 2.7x, CPU stabilized.
support-jen: prepping customer comms for affected customers (AcmeCorp, NotifierProd). ETA for next update 30m.
sre-lead: next steps: monitor for 15m, if stable expand policy globally in 3 waves (eu->ap->us). If traffic returns to >4x, escalate to full-block on UA and widen IP blocks.
cm-ops: any CX escalations? None yet beyond the support tickets. Keep me posted.
oncall-ryan: handing off active watch to @lee-sre. I'll remain available for questions. :thumbsup:
lee-sre: acknowledged, taking watch. Please tag me on any new alerts.
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-042 status: watch -> mitigated (partial). Next update in 30m or on change.
